To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Edoxaban, an oral anticoagulant, has a better net benefit than aspirin, aspirin plus Clopidogrel, or no treatment, and is likely to have better net benefit than anti-platelet treatment in both clinical trial and'real world' populations.
Edoxaban is likely to be superior to anti-platelets in reducing stroke risk and intracranial haemmorhage in both clinical trial and community populations.
edoxaban provides a positive net clinical benefit compared to anti- platelet drugs or placebo in both clinical trial and unselected community cohorts.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential for edoxaban to provide improved stroke protection and NCB in patients with non-valvular AF.
the clinical and economic impact of stroke and other thromboembolic events in patients with AF.
the potential benefits and harms of edoxaban compared to anti- platelet agents and non-treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
edoxaban is a better choice than aspirin alone, anti-platelet therapy, or no OAC in the management of patients with AF.
edoxaban is superior to anti-platelets and non-treatment for stroke prevention in AF.
the NCB of edoxaban 30 mg and 60 mg are superior to anti-platelets and placebo in both clinical trial and real-world populations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
edoxaban is a better treatment option than no treatment or treatment with anti-platelets for stroke prevention in patients with AF.
edoxaban is the best treatment for patients with non-valvular AF.
edoxaban brings a positive NCB in the prevention of thromboembolic stroke in patients with non-valvular AF, even compared to anti- platelet drugs or placebo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
edoxaban, as compared with placebo, aspirin and aspirin plus aspirin, is likely to provide better protection from stroke, ICH and death in both clinical trials and'real world' populations.
edoxaban, in the dose and dosing schedule recommended in clinical trials, is likely to provide better protection from stroke, ICH and all-cause mortality than aspirin, clopidogrel or no treatment.
edoxaban is a better choice than no treatment or aspirin for stroke prevention in non-valvular AF patients.
